How high are the Ouzoud waterfalls?
faq.answer: The falls drop about 110 metres in several tiers into the El Abid river gorge, which makes them the highest waterfalls in Morocco and among the most impressive in North Africa. The name comes from the Amazigh (Berber) word for olives, after the olive groves that surround the falls.

faq.question: What time does the tour start and end?
faq.answer: Pick-up at your hotel or riad in Marrakech is usually at 8:00, and you are back around 18:30. As the tour is private, you can start earlier to avoid the busiest hours at the falls, or later if you prefer; just tell us when you book.

faq.question: Is the local guide at the falls included?
faq.answer: Yes. A local guide meets you at Ouzoud and walks with you to the viewpoints, down to the foot of the falls and up the other side of the gorge. Guides know the safest paths, the best photo spots and where the macaques usually are. Your driver waits for you at the village.

faq.question: How much does the raft ride cost?
faq.answer: The short ride on a flat boat near the foot of the falls costs a small fee paid in cash to the boatmen, usually a few tens of dirhams per person. It's optional, takes about 15 minutes and brings you close to the spray of the cascades.

faq.question: Is the tour suitable for older travellers or people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Yes, with some adaptations. The upper viewpoints are easy to reach and offer the classic view of the falls. The full walk down to the river and back up has many steps and can be slippery, so your guide can shorten it or choose the gentlest route. Tell us when you book, and we'll plan the visit around your group.
